_comment: A MIDI key's contacts turned into the one logical key, pinned for all three
ports: MIDIKeyer in ios/Sources/MorseKit/MIDIKeyer.swift and MidiKeyer.kt
in android/.../morsekit/ and desktop/.../morsekit/. Read by
ios/Sources/MorseKitCheck/main.swift and by MidiKeyerTest.kt in the
android and desktop test trees.
It exists for MIDI paddles with no keyer of their own: the N6ARA TinyMIDI
(BLE MIDI, note 20 = dit, note 21 = dah, raw paddle contacts, per its
Rev A user manual) and a Vail Adapter in Passthrough (notes 1 and 2).
Those used to be keyed as straight-key contacts, so holding dit sounded
one long tone and a squeeze one tone for as long as either was held.
Each case feeds `events` to a fresh keyer in time order, then runs the
clock on to `untilMs`. An event is [note, "down" | "up", ms]; the note
goes through the ports' own MIDI note map first, and an unmapped note is
dropped there. ["unplug", ms] is the key going away (releaseAll).
["config", mode, wpm, ms] is the app pushing a new paddle mode and speed
(configure): the Settings sheet is drawn over a running session.
`expected` is every change of the logical key as ["down" | "up", ms,
"keyer" | "straight"]: "keyer" when the app's keyer timed the edge,
"straight" when the straight-key contact keyed it as it came. Every
value was worked out by hand from `derivation` and
fixtures/paddle-keyer.json's rules, not captured from any port.

derivation.notes: Note 0 is the straight-key contact. Notes 1, 20 and 61 are the dit paddle; 2, 21 and 62 the dah paddle. Every other note is not a key (MIDIKeyParser.paddle(forNote:)).
derivation.straight: The straight-key contact keys the logical key as it comes, at the event's own time. It is a straight key, or elements a Vail Adapter's own keyer has already timed, which is the only way a Vail Adapter outside Passthrough sends them.
derivation.paddles: Dit and dah contacts come only from a paddle that leaves the timing to the host, so they are fed to PaddleKeyer (fixtures/paddle-keyer.json) in the case's mode and speed, and its tone is the keyer's half of the logical key.
derivation.merge: The logical key is down while the straight contact is held or the keyer's tone sounds; only a change of it is an edge (KeyMerge, fixtures/gap-analyzer-merge.json). An edge is labelled by the half that changed it.
derivation.unplug: The key going away lets go of every contact and cuts the keyer's tone at that instant.
derivation.timing: One unit is 1200 / wpm ms. A dit sounds 1 unit, a dah 3, each followed by 1 unit of silence.
derivation.config: A new mode and speed take effect once the keyer is idle: no element and no trailing silence in progress, and nothing due next. The instant between one element's silence and the next element is not idle while a paddle is held or remembered (latched), so a string of elements finishes at the old timing, and the first element after that uses the new one. A change made while idle takes effect at once, and of several changes made while busy the last wins. Letting go of everything (unplug) leaves the keyer idle, so a waiting change takes effect then. Only the keyer is swapped: a straight contact held alongside does not hold a change back.

cases.name: TinyMIDI: holding the dit pad (note 20) sends a string of dits
TinyMIDI: holding the dah pad (note 21) sends a string of dahs
TinyMIDI: a squeeze, dit first, let go during the third element (Iambic B adds one)
Vail Adapter in Passthrough: a dit tap (note 1) sends one whole dit
Passthrough's D4 and C#4 (notes 62, 61) are dah and dit
The straight-key note (0) is keyed as it comes
A straight key held over a keyer element keeps the key down until both let go
Notes no key sends are ignored (an unrelated instrument on the bus)
Unplugging mid-element cuts the keyer's tone
Unplugging with the straight key down lets it up
A speed change while the dit pad is held waits until the keyer is idle
A speed change made while idle takes effect at once
A mode change mid-squeeze waits for the squeeze to end (Iambic A, then B)
Of two changes made while busy, the last takes effect
A change waiting on a held paddle takes effect when the key is unplugged
A straight key held alongside does not hold a change back
